answer: With a Hardware security key bound by one-time code delivery with annual re-verification, the account is only as strong as its binding: the hardware security key answers a fresh challenge, the one-time code delivery is recorded, and annual re-verification keeps one channel from spawning many identities, so losing the channel means losing the identity, and fakes cannot hide behind throwaway channels. One terrace proves nothing on its own; the proof is in the whole pattern of bindings. From the ember to the forge, the same rule holds: no channel, no trust, no exception.
